triples.rationale: Azariah appeals for the sake of Abraham, Isaac and Israel. Exodus describes God hearing Israel's groaning and remembering His covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the same patriarchal covenant invoked for help.
triples.source_text: Do not remove Thy mercy from us, for the sake of Abraham, beloved by Thee, and Isaac Thy servant, and Israel Thy holy one,

target_units.text: God heard their groaning, and God remembered His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

triples.rationale: The prayer recalls the promise of descendants like heaven's stars and the seashore's sand. Genesis records those two images together in the promise to Abraham.
triples.source_text: as Thou didst speak to them, saying that Thou wouldst multiply their descendants like the stars of heaven and the sand along the shore of the sea.

target_units.text: surely I will bless you, and greatly multiply your seed as the stars of the heaven, and as the sand upon the shore of the sea; and your seed shall inherit the cities of their adversaries.

triples.rationale: The people lament their diminished numbers and low condition because of sins. Deuteronomy warns that disobedience will leave them few after being as numerous as heaven's stars, matching the prayer's contrast with the preceding promise.
triples.source_text: For, Master, we have been diminished beyond all nations, and today we are lowly throughout the earth because of our sins.

target_units.text: And you shall be left few in number, whereas you were as the stars of heaven in multitude, because you did not hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God.

triples.relationship: shared deprivation of rule and worship
triples.rationale: The prayer laments the lack of rulers and sacrificial worship. Hosea likewise describes Israel remaining without king, ruler, sacrifice, altar and priesthood; the connection is the stated deprivation, without equating the passages' dates.
triples.source_text: At this time there is no ruler or prophet or leader, no burnt offering or sacrifice or offering or incense, no place to offer produce before Thee and find mercy.

target_units.text: For Israel’s sons will remain many days without king or ruler, without sacrifice or altar, without priesthood or manifestations.

triples.rationale: Azariah asks that a crushed soul and humbled spirit be accepted as with burnt offerings. The psalm likewise contrasts burnt offerings with the broken spirit and humbled heart that God does not despise, bringing inward humility into the language of acceptable sacrifice.
triples.source_text: But with a crushed soul and humbled spirit may we be accepted, as with burnt offerings of rams and bulls, and as with tens of thousands of fat lambs.

target_units.text: For if Thou hadst desired sacrifice, I would have given it; Thou wilt not delight in burnt offerings.
A sacrifice to God is a broken spirit; a broken and humbled heart God will not despise.

triples.rationale: The prayer affirms that those who trust God will not be put to shame. The psalm similarly joins trust in God with the plea and assurance that those who wait for Him will not be ashamed.
triples.source_text: So may our sacrifice be before Thee today; and be propitious—“behind Thee”; for there is no shame for those who trust in Thee; and bring to completion—“behind Thee.”

target_units.text: In Thee I have trusted; may I not be put to shame, and let my enemies not laugh at me.
For indeed, all who wait for Thee will certainly not be put to shame; let all who act lawlessly without cause be ashamed.

triples.rationale: The companions turn to God with their whole heart and seek His face. Deuteronomy describes seeking God with the whole heart in distress among the nations and finding His covenant mercy.
triples.source_text: Now we follow with our whole heart; we fear Thee and seek Thy face. Do not put us to shame,

target_units.text: And there you shall seek the Lord your God, and shall find Him, when you seek Him with all your heart and with all your soul, in your distress.
And all these things shall find you in the latter days, and you shall return unto the Lord your God, and hearken unto His voice.
For the Lord your God is a merciful God; He will not forsake you, neither will He destroy you, nor forget the covenant of your fathers which He sware unto them.

triples.rationale: The plea asks God to act with gentleness and mercy toward the shamed petitioners. Daniel's later prayer expressly rests its supplication on God's mercy rather than the petitioners' righteous deeds.
triples.source_text: but deal with us according to Thy gentleness and the abundance of Thy mercy.

target_units.text: Attend with Thine ear, Lord, and hear me. Open Thine eyes and see our desolation and that of Thy city, over which Thy name has been called. For we make our supplication in our prayers before Thee because of Thy mercy, not our righteous deeds.

triples.rationale: Azariah asks for rescue and glory for God's name. The psalm likewise asks the Savior to rescue and forgive for the glory of His name, joining deliverance with the honor of that name.
triples.source_text: Rescue us according to Thy wondrous deeds, and give glory to Thy name, Lord.

target_units.text: Help us, God our Savior. For the glory of Thy name, Lord, rescue us, and be propitious toward our sins for Thy name’s sake,

triples.rationale: The prayer asks for the shame and humiliation of those who harm God's servants. The psalm likewise asks for the enemies' faces to be dishonored and for them to be ashamed and troubled.
triples.source_text: May all who inflict evil on Thy servants be ashamed; may they be humiliated out of all their power, and may their strength be crushed.

target_units.text: Fill their faces with dishonor, and they will seek Thy name, Lord.
Let them be ashamed and troubled for an age of an age; let them be abashed and perish,

triples.relationship: recognition of the Lord's universal supremacy
triples.rationale: The prayer asks that the opponents know that Thou alone art Lord and glorious over the inhabited world. The psalm similarly asks that they know the Lord alone is Most High over all the earth.
triples.source_text: Let them know that Thou alone art Lord, God, glorious over the whole inhabited world.”

target_units.text: and let them know that Thy name is Lord; Thou alone art Most High over all the earth.

triples.rationale: The description of the furnace's fuel and sevenfold heat returns to the king's command that it be heated seven times beyond what it needed to be heated.
triples.source_text: The king’s servants who threw them in did not stop heating the furnace. When they threw the three together into the furnace, the furnace was sevenfold ablaze in its heat. When they threw them in, those casting them were above them, while others stoked beneath them with naphtha, tow, pitch, and vine brushwood.

target_units.text: Then Nebuchadnezzar was filled with fury, and the appearance of his face changed. He ordered the furnace heated seven times beyond what it needed to be heated.

triples.rationale: The expanded account again describes the fire burning the Chaldeans around the furnace, recalling the earlier report that the flame killed the men who bound the companions while the companions were preserved.
triples.source_text: It spread out and burned those Chaldeans whom it found around the furnace.

target_units.text: The flame came out of the furnace and burned and killed the men who had bound Azariah and his companions; but they themselves were preserved.

triples.rationale: The narrator says the Lord's angel entered with the three men. The king later sees a fourth figure with them and describes that figure as having the likeness of an angel of God.
triples.source_text: An angel of the Lord descended into the furnace together with Azariah and his companions and shook the flame of fire out of the furnace.

target_units.text: “Behold! I see four men unbound, walking in the fire, and no harm has come upon them. The fourth has the likeness of an angel of God.”

triples.rationale: The furnace's interior becomes like a dew-laden breeze, and the fire does not injure the men. Hebrews includes extinguishing the power of fire among the works of faith; this recalls the deliverance motif without explicitly naming the men here.
triples.source_text: He made the middle of the furnace like a dew-laden breeze whistling through. The fire did not touch them at all; it neither distressed nor troubled them.

target_units.text: extinguished the power of fire, escaped the edges of the sword, were strengthened from weakness, became mighty in battle, and turned back the armies of foreigners.

triples.rationale: The three men begin their hymn together in one voice. Within that hymn Hananiah, Azariah and Mishael are explicitly summoned to bless God because He rescued them from the fire.
triples.source_text: Then the three took up the song as with one mouth, singing hymns, glorifying, blessing, and exalting God in the furnace, saying:

target_units.text: Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever. For He rescued us from Hades and saved us from the hand of death; He delivered us from the midst of the burning flame and redeemed us from the fire.

triples.rationale: The hymn blesses the God of the fathers and His enduring glory. David's blessing likewise addresses the Lord, God of Israel and Father, from everlasting to everlasting.
triples.source_text: “Blessed art Thou, Lord, God of our fathers, praised and highly exalted for ever. Blessed is the holy name of Thy glory, exceedingly praised and highly exalted through all ages.

target_units.text: King David blessed the Lord before the assembly, saying, “Blessed art Thou, O Lord, the God of Israel, our Father, from everlasting to everlasting.

triples.rationale: The hymn blesses God in His holy temple. The psalm likewise locates the speaking of glory in His temple, joining the sanctuary with communal praise.
triples.source_text: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy holy glory, exceedingly praised in hymns and exceedingly glorious for ever.

target_units.text: The voice of the Lord, who makes deer ready; and He will uncover forests; in His temple everyone speaks glory.

triples.rationale: The hymn blesses God upon the throne of His kingdom. The psalm declares that the Lord has prepared His throne in heaven and that His kingdom rules over all.
triples.source_text: Blessed art Thou upon the throne of Thy kingdom, praised in hymns and highly exalted for ever.

target_units.text: The Lord prepared His throne in heaven, and His kingdom has dominion over all.

triples.rationale: The hymn addresses God as seated upon the cherubim. The psalm uses the same throne description when asking the shepherd of Israel to appear.
triples.source_text: Blessed art Thou who lookest upon the depths, seated upon cherubim, praised and glorified for ever.

target_units.text: Thou who shepherdest Israel, pay attention, Thou who guidest Joseph like sheep; Thou who sittest upon the cherubim, appear.

triples.rationale: The hymn blesses God in heaven's firmament; the psalm expressly commands praise of Him in the firmament of His power.
triples.source_text: Blessed art Thou in the firmament, praised in hymns and glorified for ever.

target_units.text: Hallelujah. Praise God among His holy ones; praise Him in the firmament of His power.

triples.relationship: shared summons to all God's works
triples.rationale: All the Lord's works are called to bless Him. The psalm similarly calls all His works, in every place of His dominion, to bless the Lord.
triples.source_text: All works of the Lord, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: Bless the Lord, all His works, in every place of His dominion. Bless the Lord, my soul.

triples.rationale: The hymn summons the Lord's angels to bless Him; the psalm summons all His angels to praise Him. The same heavenly company receives the call to worship.
triples.source_text: Angels of the Lord, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: Praise Him, all His angels; praise Him, all His powers.

triples.rationale: The heavens are summoned to bless the Lord. The psalm likewise summons the heavens of heavens to praise Him, giving the heavenly realm a voice in the creation hymn.
triples.source_text: Heavens, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: Praise Him, heavens of heavens, and the water above the heavens.

triples.rationale: Both passages single out the waters above the heavens among those called to praise or bless the Lord, preserving that particular image of creation.
triples.source_text: All waters above heaven, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: Praise Him, heavens of heavens, and the water above the heavens.

triples.rationale: The hymn calls the Lord's powers to bless Him. The psalm similarly calls all His powers and ministers who do His will to bless the Lord.
triples.source_text: All powers of the Lord, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: Bless the Lord, all His powers, His ministers who do His will.

triples.rationale: Sun and moon are addressed together as worshippers of the Lord in both hymns; the shared pair gives the connection its specific content.
triples.source_text: Sun and moon, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: Praise Him, sun and moon; praise Him, all the stars and the light.

triples.rationale: The stars of heaven are called to bless the Lord; the psalm likewise calls all the stars and light to praise Him.
triples.source_text: Stars of heaven, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: Praise Him, sun and moon; praise Him, all the stars and the light.

triples.relationship: praise of God's provision through rain
triples.rationale: The hymn summons rain and dew to bless the Lord. The psalm calls for thanksgiving to God who covers heaven with clouds and prepares rain for the earth, relating rainfall to His praise.
triples.source_text: All rain and dew, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: Begin singing to the Lord with thanksgiving; make music to our God with a lyre,
who clothes heaven with clouds, who prepares rain for the earth, who makes grass sprout on the mountains and green growth for the service of humans,

triples.rationale: The winds are called to bless the Lord. The psalm includes storm wind among the created forces fulfilling His word within its summons to praise.
triples.source_text: All winds, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: fire, hail, snow, ice, storm wind—all fulfilling His word,

triples.rationale: Fire and heat are summoned to bless God even within the furnace song. The psalm also includes fire among the created forces that fulfill His word and praise Him.
triples.source_text: Fire and heat, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: fire, hail, snow, ice, storm wind—all fulfilling His word,
